experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for a late Day 1 arrival — simply drop bags at a Lagos-based hotel and walk to the beach. Calm waters, golden sand, and beachside bars make it perfect for unwinding after a long flight without needing transport.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Stay in Carvoeiro or Lagoa to be within 10 minutes of this spot, avoiding long transfers. Morning visits offer calmer waters and fewer crowds, perfect for snorkeling and cliff photography.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood and cheeses. Sessions typically run 2–3 hours and are hosted mid-morning, making them ideal for Day 2 or 3 when you are fully settled. Book a hotel in Lagoa or Silves to be within 15 minutes of multiple quintas.

experiences.name: Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and wander the cobblestone streets of Portugal's former Algarve capital. Combine culture with food by joining a guided walking tour that stops at local taverns for regional wines, cataplana seafood stew, and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally located and easily reachable from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels in under 20 minutes, keeping transfers short and maximizing your day.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the famous Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours last approximately 2 hours and depart in the morning when seas are calmest. Stay in Carvoeiro, just 5 km away, to avoid long travel and ensure you catch the early morning slot before afternoon winds pick up. A highlight activity well within budget.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Eva Bus or Rede Expressos coach from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. €5-7, ~1.5 hours). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva. Freshen up and get settled.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24h mini-market or a kebab/pizza slice shop near the hostel in Lagos town center (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage light for the bus journey. Buy bus tickets at the Faro Airport bus terminal. The hostel is walkable from Lagos bus station (~10 min walk or a short €5 taxi ride). Get a good night's rest — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and explore Lagos old town on foot. Walk the historic town walls, visit Igreja de Santa Maria, and stroll through Praça Gil Eanes. Pick up a free map from the hostel and orient yourself to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach (a 20-minute walk or short bus ride, €1.50). This long, calm sandy beach is perfect for a first swim. Rent a beach umbrella and chair for ~€5-8. Explore the beach and enjoy the warm September Atlantic waters.
day_by_day.evening: Walk back into Lagos old town. Explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril for bars and restaurants. Enjoy the sunset from the Ponta da Bandeira Fort viewpoint (free from outside).

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a pastel de nata and coffee at a local café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed sandwich from a local padaria (bakery) near the hostel (~€3-4)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or a local tasca near the old town — try grilled sardines or prego sandwich (~€8-12)

day_by_day.notes: September weather in Algarve is typically warm (24-28°C) with low chance of rain — ideal beach weather. Bring sunscreen and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Ponta da Piedade — a stunning sea stack and cave formation just 2km south of Lagos. Walk or rent a bike (~€10/day from local shops near the hostel). Arrive early to beat crowds and enjoy the golden cliffs in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the steps at Ponta da Piedade to Praia do Camilo, a small hidden beach nestled between dramatic cliffs. Swim and relax. Alternatively, take a budget kayak tour of the sea caves from the beach (~€15-20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Walk along the marina and watch the fishing boats come in. Browse the evening market stalls if running.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at Café Conchinha or similar local café in Lagos (~€3)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch — buy fresh bread, local cheese, olives, and fruit from the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (~€5-6 total)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the waterfront — try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or grilled fish (~€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is free to visit. The kayak tours are best booked the morning of or the day before. Wear sturdy sandals for the cliff steps.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres — take the Eva Bus from Lagos bus station (~€4.50 each way, ~1 hour). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), the most southwestern point of continental Europe. Walk the windswept cliffs and enjoy breathtaking Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes from Sagres to Praia do Martinhal or Praia da Mareta — two beautiful, sheltered beaches near Sagres town. Swim and relax on the quieter, less-touristy sands.
day_by_day.evening: Return bus to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the hostel common area, meet fellow travelers, and plan the next few days.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or grab a pastel de nata at the bus station café (~€2)
meals.lunch: A Sagres restaurant near the fortress — try a bifana (pork sandwich) or soup of the day (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Nah Nah Bah burger bar in Lagos old town — great value burgers and craft beer (~€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: Check the Eva Bus schedule in advance at the Lagos bus terminal. Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. The Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse is a 6km walk or taxi (~€8) from Sagres if you want to visit the westernmost point of Europe.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a morning bus or rideshare to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (~30 min from Lagos, taxi ~€20 or arrange a shared tour). Enjoy a guided vineyard tour and wine tasting of Algarve regional wines including Negra Mole and Syrah blends (~€15-20 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue wine exploration at Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery) near Guia, or return toward Lagos and visit a local wine shop for a self-guided tasting of Algarve wines. Pick up a bottle of local wine for ~€5-8.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy your purchased wine on the hostel terrace or rooftop if available. Socialize with other hostel guests.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel before departure (~€3-5 or included)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery or a nearby village café — try local bread with queijo fresco and presunto (~€7-9)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — traditional Portuguese petiscos (tapas-style small plates) great for sharing (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Book winery tours in advance, especially on weekends. Some wineries offer free or discounted tours if you purchase wine. Consider grouping with other hostel guests to share taxi costs.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Luz, a charming beach village 6km west of Lagos. Take the local bus (€1.50) or walk along the coastal path (~1.5 hours scenic walk). The beach here is wide, calm, and less crowded than central Lagos beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a SUP (stand-up paddleboard) or bodyboard at Praia da Luz (~€10-15/hour). Explore the red-ochre cliffs from the water. Alternatively, simply relax on the beach and swim.
day_by_day.evening: Walk or bus back to Lagos. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) — the only remaining slave market building in Europe (€3 entry, closes around 18:00). Reflect on the sobering history.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Luz — grilled chicken piri-piri or fresh salad (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos — a beloved local spot with daily specials and generous portions (~€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday can be quieter for transport — check bus schedules. The coastal walk from Lagos to Praia da Luz is beautiful but bring water and sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha. Take the train from Lagos to Portimão (€2.30, ~20 min) — one of the cheapest and most scenic rail routes in Algarve. Walk from Portimão station to Praia da Rocha (~20 min) — a wide, dramatic beach backed by golden cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the beach and swim. Walk the clifftop promenade above Praia da Rocha for panoramic views. Visit the Fortaleza de Santa Catarina (free entry) at the eastern end of the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Portimão town center. Browse the riverside fish market area and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Take the train back to Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at Lagos train station café (~€2)
meals.lunch: Portimão is famous for grilled sardines — eat at one of the riverside tascas near the fish market (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: O Trovador restaurant in Lagos old town — traditional bacalhau (salt cod) dishes at budget prices (~€9-13)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos-Portimão train runs regularly. Keep your train ticket for the return journey. Portimão also has a good supermarket (Pingo Doce) if you need to stock up on supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the hidden beaches west of Lagos on foot or by bike. Cycle or walk the coastal path to Praia do Porto de Mós (~3km from Lagos). This semi-secluded beach has dramatic cliff formations and clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coastal path to Praia do Pinhão — a tiny, sheltered cove accessible by steep wooden steps. One of the most picturesque beaches near Lagos. Swim and explore the rock pools.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Visit the local Mercado Municipal for fresh produce. Cook a simple meal in the hostel kitchen (if available) using local ingredients — a great budget option.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic from the market — local cheese, olives, tomatoes, bread (~€5)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hostel kitchen meal — fresh pasta with local clams (ameijoas) bought from the market (~€6-8 total) OR Restaurante Bon Vivant for affordable daily specials (~€9-11)

day_by_day.notes: The coastal path between Lagos beaches can be uneven — wear proper footwear. Bring plenty of water as there are no facilities between some beaches. This is a great day for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Take the train from Lagos to Tunes, then change for Silves (total ~€4, ~45 min). Visit the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — visit the Gothic Cathedral (free), browse the local craft shops, and walk along the Arade River. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (€2) for fascinating Moorish history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Enjoy a quiet evening stroll along the Lagos waterfront and marina.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at Lagos train station (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — a charming café below the castle walls with affordable lunch specials (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — try arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a highlight of the Algarve interior and often overlooked by beach tourists. The train journey through orange and almond groves is scenic. Check return train times before you go.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Herdade dos Pimenteiros or a local Lagos wine bar for a morning tasting session of Algarve DOC wines. Many wine shops in Lagos old town offer informal tastings for free or ~€5-10.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Meia Praia Beach — the longest beach near Lagos (4km of sand). Take the small ferry from Lagos marina to Meia Praia (€1 each way) for a fun, cheap crossing. Spend the afternoon swimming and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beach bar on Meia Praia or return to Lagos for happy hour at one of the old town bars (many offer 2-for-1 drinks 17:00-19:00).

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Meia Praia — grilled fish of the day or salad (~€9-11)
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos or similar seafood restaurant in Lagos — fresh grilled sea bream (dourada) (~€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: The Meia Praia ferry is a fun local experience and very cheap. The beach is popular with locals and less touristy than central Lagos beaches. Great for a relaxed, unhurried day.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Albufeira — take the train from Lagos (€5.50, ~1 hour). Explore the old town, the famous Fisherman's Beach (Praia dos Pescadores), and the clifftop viewpoints. Albufeira is livelier and more touristy but worth a visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a local bus to Praia da Oura or Praia de Santa Eulália — wider, less crowded beaches east of Albufeira. Swim and enjoy the afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by train. Friday evening in Lagos old town is lively — enjoy the street atmosphere, live music, and browse the night market if running.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at Lagos station (~€2)
meals.lunch: Albufeira old town — try a piri-piri chicken wrap or fresh fish at a local tasca (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mullens in Lagos — popular with locals and travelers, great value grills (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is more expensive and touristy than Lagos — stick to local tascas away from the main strip for better value. The train journey along the Algarve coast is scenic and relaxing.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach from the trip (Ponta da Piedade area, Praia do Camilo, or Meia Praia). Spend a leisurely morning swimming, snorkeling, or simply relaxing on the sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for last-minute souvenir shopping in the old town. Visit the local craft market or browse shops on Rua 25 de Abril for affordable Portuguese souvenirs — local wine, ginjinha, ceramic tiles, cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos. Splurge slightly on a nicer meal to celebrate the end of the trip. Walk the illuminated old town walls at night for a magical final evening.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or a special sit-down breakfast at a café (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Beach picnic — final market haul of local produce, wine, and bread (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos — a slightly upscale but still affordable traditional Portuguese restaurant, perfect for a farewell meal (~€15-20 as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight and set an alarm for tomorrow. Check bus/train times to Faro Airport. Leave a review for the hostel if you enjoyed your stay — it helps other budget travelers!

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Store luggage at the hostel if your departure is later. Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town — visit the fish market one last time, grab a final pastel de nata and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: take the Eva Bus or Rede Expressos from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~€5-7, ~1.5 hours). Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches and wines of the Algarve!

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão (milky coffee) at a Lagos café — a perfect Portuguese farewell (~€3)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Lagos or Faro Airport — sandwich or soup (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details the night before. The Lagos to Faro Airport bus runs several times daily — check the exact schedule at the Lagos bus terminal or online at rede-expressos.pt. Keep €10-15 cash for any last-minute transport or airport expenses.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Take the airport shuttle or a pre-booked taxi (~1 hour) to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos. Check in, freshen up, and grab a light snack if the hostel bar is still open.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Pick up a late-night snack at a 24-hour petrol station convenience store en route, or check if the hostel has snacks available at check-in

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid waiting at night. Keep luggage light for easy check-in. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a short walk to explore Lagos old town — stroll along the historic city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António, and get oriented with your surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach Day — one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, just a 10-minute taxi or bike ride from Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed first swim in the Atlantic, sunbathe on the wide sandy shore, and rent a sun lounger.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos and wander the lively Rua 25 de Abril for bar-hopping and a casual dinner. Enjoy the vibrant nightlife scene that Lagos is famous for.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or a nearby pastelaria near the hostel — coffee, pastel de nata, and fresh orange juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Meia Praia — grilled sardines, prego sandwich, or a fresh salad (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: O Camilo or Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — grilled fish of the day, local wine, and dessert (~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is ideal for first-timers — calm waters, easy access, and facilities. Bring sunscreen, as September sun in the Algarve is still strong.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat tour from Lagos Marina departing around 9:30am. Explore the famous sea caves, grottos, and golden rock arches of Ponta da Piedade — one of the most iconic coastal landscapes in Portugal.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the boat tour, walk down to Praia do Camilo or Praia de Dona Ana — two stunning small coves near Lagos accessible by steps carved into the cliffs. Swim and relax in the sheltered turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Head back into Lagos town centre for a sunset aperitivo. Visit the Mercado de Lagos (if open late) or enjoy drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the marina.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or Pastelaria Mira Mar near the marina — toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6–9)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia de Dona Ana or pack a picnic from a local deli — cheese, cured meats, bread, and local wine (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — traditional Algarvian cataplana (seafood stew), local Algarve wine (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ponta da Piedade boat tour in advance — September is still busy. Tours typically last 45–75 minutes and cost €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take a local bus or rent a car for the ~30-minute drive inland. Start with the Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk: explore the impressive red sandstone Moorish castle, walk the cobblestone streets, and visit the Silves Cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Silves food walk through the old town, sampling local specialties — medronho (arbutus berry brandy), almond sweets, and smoked sausages from artisan shops. Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia for a dose of history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by early evening. Relax at the hostel, then head out for a quieter dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Silves town square — coffee and local pastries upon arrival (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for grilled fish and seafood, a local institution (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: A Forja restaurant in Lagos — rustic Portuguese home cooking, petiscos (tapas-style small plates), local wine (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the most historically rich towns in the Algarve. The castle entrance fee is ~€3. Wear comfortable shoes for the cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus west toward Sagres (~45 minutes from Lagos). Visit the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Walk the clifftops and visit the lighthouse with sweeping Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta near Sagres — wild, windswept beaches with a raw, unspoiled feel. Swim and explore the rugged coastline. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress) for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for dinner. Enjoy a relaxed evening stroll along the marina waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Grab coffee and a pastel de nata from a café near the hostel before departing (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante in Sagres — fresh seafood with ocean views, grilled sea bass or tuna (~€20–28 per person)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Lagos — cosy local tasca with daily specials, affordable and authentic (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The drive along the Costa Vicentina is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience — join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa (~30 minutes from Lagos by car). Learn about Algarve's four wine regions, taste local varietals including Negra Mole and Arinto, paired with regional cheeses and cured meats.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine experience, explore the charming town of Lagoa — visit the Igreja Matriz, browse local shops, and pick up a bottle or two of Algarve wine to take home. Optionally visit Carvoeiro village and its small beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a nightcap at the hostel bar or a wine bar in town, reflecting on the day's tastings.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or café near the hostel — light start before the wine tasting (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Included or partially included in the wine and seafood pairing experience — charcuterie, local cheeses, bread, and paired wines (~€35–50 per person for the full experience)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro area) or a simpler option — grilled octopus salad, local wine, and dessert (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience at least 3–5 days in advance. Most quintas offer morning or early afternoon sessions. Designate a driver or arrange a taxi if you plan to taste generously.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend the morning at leisure around Lagos. Visit the Mercado Municipal de Lagos for fresh local produce, flowers, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim — drive or take a taxi (~35 minutes east of Lagos) to one of the most photographed beaches in Portugal. Walk the clifftop trail admiring the golden limestone formations, then descend to the cove for a swim in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a special mid-trip dinner. Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dining experience to celebrate the halfway point.

meals.breakfast: Mercado Municipal de Lagos — fresh fruit, local honey, artisan bread, and coffee from market stalls (~€7–10)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia da Marinha or pack a picnic — local bread, cheese, fruit, and a small bottle of Algarve wine (~€12–15)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama in Lagos — upscale-casual seafood and Portuguese cuisine, excellent wine list (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is consistently rated one of the top 10 beaches in Europe. The cliff walk is moderately easy but wear sturdy sandals or trainers. Arrive before 3pm to avoid afternoon crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip east to Portimão and Ferragudo. Start with a morning walk around the charming fishing village of Ferragudo — explore the castle ruins, whitewashed houses, and the small harbour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the river to Portimão and visit Praia da Rocha — a wide, dramatic beach backed by ochre cliffs. Swim, relax, and explore the clifftop promenade. Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays) for local history and sardine canning heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner before returning to Lagos (~20 minutes by bus or taxi).

meals.breakfast: Café in Ferragudo village square — coffee, toast with local jam, and fresh juice (~€6–8)
meals.lunch: Tasca da Dona Barca in Ferragudo — legendary grilled sardines and local fish, a true Algarvian experience (~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — modern Portuguese cuisine with local ingredients, good wine selection (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is a quieter, more authentic alternative to the busier tourist towns. The ferry crossing between Ferragudo and Portimão is a fun and cheap experience (~€1).

day_by_day.morning: Morning kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session from Lagos Beach or Meia Praia. Several operators near the marina offer 2-hour guided kayak tours along the coastline to sea caves and hidden coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hostel, shower, and spend a relaxed afternoon exploring Lagos on foot. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) — the only one of its kind in Europe — and the historic Praça Gil Eanes.
day_by_day.evening: Join a sunset sailing trip from Lagos Marina — many operators offer 2-hour sunset cruises with wine and snacks included. A perfect Algarve experience.

meals.breakfast: Café Atlântico near the marina — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto, cheese, and coffee (~€8–11)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Escondidinho in Lagos — hidden gem with daily fish specials and homemade desserts (~€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the sunset cruise — tapas and wine at a bar on Rua 25 de Abril (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kayak tours typically cost €25–35 per person. Sunset sailing cruises cost €30–45 per person and often include local wine — book 1–2 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine-focused excursion — visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar (~40 minutes from Lagos), one of the most acclaimed wine estates in the Algarve. Take a guided vineyard tour and tasting of their award-winning reds and whites.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery visit, stop at the nearby town of Estômbar or Mexilhoeira Grande for a quiet lunch. On the return, detour to Alvor — a picturesque fishing village with a beautiful estuary boardwalk and a long sandy beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a relaxed evening. Browse the evening market stalls if running, or enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hostel before departing (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Local tasca in Estômbar or Mexilhoeira Grande — pork with clams (carne de porco à alentejana), house wine (~€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Três Palmeiras in Alvor (if staying later) or back in Lagos — grilled fish, local wine, and dessert (~€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales offers sculpture gardens alongside the vineyard — a unique artistic touch. Winery tours cost approximately €15–25 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Meia Praia — return to this beloved stretch of sand for a longer, more leisurely visit. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella, swim, read, and fully unwind.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Meia Praia or take a short walk to the quieter eastern end of the beach. Try water sports — jet ski rental, windsurfing lessons, or beach volleyball are all available.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beach bar at Meia Praia before heading back to Lagos for a farewell-style dinner with fellow travellers from the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or grab pastries from a nearby padaria (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant at Meia Praia — fresh grilled fish, salad, and a cold Sagres beer (~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — lively atmosphere, excellent cataplana and grilled seafood, local wine (~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September waters in the Algarve are still warm (~22°C) — perfect for swimming. Meia Praia is ideal for water sports due to its consistent breeze.

day_by_day.morning: Final exploration day — take a morning hike along the Rota Vicentina coastal trail section near Lagos. The Fishermen's Trail offers dramatic clifftop scenery heading south toward Luz or north toward Burgau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Luz (~10 minutes west of Lagos) — a relaxed resort village with a beautiful black-sand beach (Praia da Luz) and a Roman ruins site. Swim and enjoy the calmer atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a final evening. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping — local wine, almond sweets, ceramic tiles, and cork products. Enjoy a farewell dinner at your favourite spot from the trip.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hostel — full breakfast to fuel the morning hike (~€8–11)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Fortaleza da Luz in Luz — seafood with ocean views, relaxed setting (~€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Return to your favourite Lagos restaurant from the trip — or try Restaurante Casinha do Petisco for a final cataplana experience (~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Rota Vicentina coastal trail sections near Lagos are well-marked and suitable for all fitness levels. Wear sunscreen and bring water. Praia da Luz has a lovely Roman ruins museum worth a quick visit (~€2).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos — enjoy a slow, leisurely breakfast. Take one last walk along the Lagos waterfront and marina. Pack, check out of the hostel, and store luggage if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, either relax at a café in Lagos town centre or head to Faro Airport. The drive from Lagos to Faro Airport takes approximately 1 hour — allow extra time for traffic and check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, seafood, and Algarvian sunshine.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a Lagos pastelaria — savour the moment (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near the hostel or at Faro Airport — soup, sandwich, or a snack (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most Portuguese hostels is 11am — arrange late checkout or luggage storage if needed. Pre-book your airport transfer back to Faro to avoid stress on departure day. Obrigado e boa viagem — thank you and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed afternoon at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for a late Day 1 arrival — simply drop bags at a Lagos-based hotel and walk to the beach. Calm waters, golden sand, and beachside bars make it perfect for unwinding after a long flight without needing transport.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. Stay in Carvoeiro or Lagoa to be within 10 minutes of this spot, avoiding long transfers. Morning visits offer calmer waters and fewer crowds, perfect for snorkeling and cliff photography.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a local quinta near Lagoa, the heart of Algarve wine country, sampling regional Negra Mole and Arinto wines paired with fresh local seafood and cheeses. Sessions typically run 2–3 hours and are hosted mid-morning, making them ideal for Day 2 or 3 when you are fully settled. Book a hotel in Lagoa or Silves to be within 15 minutes of multiple quintas.

experiences.name: Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk
experiences.description: Discover the Moorish Silves Castle and wander the cobblestone streets of Portugal's former Algarve capital. Combine culture with food by joining a guided walking tour that stops at local taverns for regional wines, cataplana seafood stew, and medronho brandy. Silves is centrally located and easily reachable from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels in under 20 minutes, keeping transfers short and maximizing your day.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the famous Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most spectacular natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Tours last approximately 2 hours and depart in the morning when seas are calmest. Stay in Carvoeiro, just 5 km away, to avoid long travel and ensure you catch the early morning slot before afternoon winds pick up. A highlight activity well within budget.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A pre-arranged private transfer (Mercedes E-Class or similar) whisks you to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel. Light late-night snack from the hotel's curated welcome basket.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack basket at hotel (charcuterie, local cheese, Algarve wine)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long-haul flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then take a gentle orientation stroll through Lagos old town — explore the historic city walls, Praça Gil Eanes, and the charming cobblestone lanes. Visit the Igreja de Santo António, a stunning baroque church. Pick up a pastel de nata from a local bakery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia Beach Day — one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, just a short taxi or hotel shuttle ride from Lagos. Settle into a premium sun lounger, swim in the calm Atlantic waters, and enjoy the wide golden sands. Rent a paddleboard or kayak for a gentle afternoon on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace or a rooftop bar overlooking the marina. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant such as No Pátio or Casinha do Petisco — expect fresh grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco, and a bottle of chilled Alvarinho.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — fresh bread, local jams, cheese, presunto, fresh orange juice, espresso
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Meia Praia's premium beach restaurant — grilled prawns, fresh salads, local white wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at No Pátio Lagos — tasting menu with local seafood, paired with Algarve and Alentejo wines (~€60–80pp)

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is approximately 3 km from Lagos centre — a short taxi or hotel-arranged transfer. September weather is typically warm (24–28°C) with calm seas. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, arrange a private driver or hire a car for the day. Head east along the coast to the Praia da Marinha Cliff Walk and Swim. Arrive early to beat any crowds and begin the iconic cliff-top trail, marvelling at the dramatic golden limestone formations, sea arches, and hidden coves. The walk takes approximately 1.5–2 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha's crystal-clear turquoise cove for a swim in one of the Algarve's most celebrated beaches. The water is exceptionally clear in September. Explore the smaller adjacent coves by swimming or snorkelling. Pack a premium picnic from a Lagos deli or stop at a nearby café.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the charming town of Carvoeiro for sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar. Dinner at Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro or Bon Bon Restaurant (Michelin-starred) in Carvoeiro — an unmissable luxury dining experience featuring creative Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Premium picnic on the cliffs or light lunch at a local café near Praia da Marinha — local cheese, smoked fish, crusty bread, local rosé
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) — tasting menu ~€120–150pp with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is approximately 35 km east of Lagos (~35 min drive). Wear sturdy walking shoes for the cliff path. The cliff walk can be uneven — take care near edges. Book Bon Bon well in advance as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart after breakfast for the Algarve Wine and Seafood Pairing Experience near Lagoa — the heart of Algarve wine country. Arrive at a local quinta (wine estate) for a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, learning about the unique Algarve terroir, indigenous grape varieties (Negra Mole, Crato Branco), and winemaking traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the experience with a curated wine and seafood pairing session — expect 5–6 wines matched with locally sourced seafood dishes: percebes (barnacles), smoked tuna, grilled octopus, and fresh oysters. The sommelier will guide you through each pairing. Browse the estate's wine shop and select bottles to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Relax at the hotel with a spa treatment if available, or enjoy a quiet evening stroll along the Lagos marina. Dinner at a relaxed but premium wine-bar-style restaurant in Lagos — try Adega da Marina for a more intimate, wine-focused dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Included as part of the wine and seafood pairing experience at the quinta
meals.dinner: Adega da Marina, Lagos — grilled fish, regional petiscos, excellent local wine list (~€45–60pp)

day_by_day.notes: Lagoa is approximately 25 km east of Lagos (~25 min drive). Book the wine and seafood pairing experience in advance — private group sessions are available for a more exclusive experience. Arrange a designated driver or private transfer for the wine tasting day.

day_by_day.morning: A free, relaxed morning in Lagos. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, then explore the Mercado Municipal de Lagos (local market) for fresh produce, local honey, almonds, and artisan goods. Visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos) — a sobering and important historical site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon at leisure on Praia Dona Ana — one of Lagos's most beautiful and accessible beaches, just a short walk or taxi from the hotel. The dramatic amber cliffs frame a sheltered cove perfect for swimming. Hire a private boat tour from Lagos marina to explore the sea caves and grottos along the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar above Praia Dona Ana. Dinner at Restaurante Vasco da Gama or a premium seafood restaurant on the Lagos waterfront — try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or whole grilled turbot.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast, followed by market pastries and espresso
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — fresh fruit, local charcuterie, and a glass of chilled vinho verde from a beachside kiosk
meals.dinner: Premium waterfront seafood restaurant in Lagos (~€55–75pp with wine)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets in Lagos are lively — arrive by 9:30am for the best selection. Private boat tours from Lagos marina can be booked on the day or in advance — 2-hour tours typically cost €40–60pp, or hire a private vessel for ~€200–300.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, drive or arrange a private transfer to Silves for the Silves Castle and Old Town Food Walk. Begin at the magnificent Moorish Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) — one of the best-preserved Moorish fortifications in Portugal. Explore the red sandstone ramparts, towers, and cisterns with a private guide for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a guided food walk through Silves' cobblestone old town. Sample local specialities: smoked sausages, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), local Silves oranges, artisan cheeses, and traditional medronho (arbutus berry spirit). Visit the Silves Cathedral and browse the artisan shops. Stop at a local tasca for a traditional lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos via a scenic drive through the Algarve hinterland — rolling hills, cork oak forests, and orange groves. Evening at leisure. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Lagos or a private chef experience arranged through the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a Silves tasca — pork cheeks (bochechas de porco), local bread, house wine (~€25–35pp)
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the hotel or fine dining at a Lagos restaurant — request the hotel concierge to arrange (~€80–120pp for private chef)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 35 km northeast of Lagos (~35 min drive). A private guide for the castle and food walk can be arranged through the hotel concierge — highly recommended for a richer experience. The castle entrance fee is approximately €3pp.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Portimão and Praia da Rocha for a change of scenery. Explore the dramatic rock formations and wide sandy beach of Praia da Rocha. Walk the clifftop promenade for panoramic views. Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) — an award-winning museum housed in a former sardine canning factory.
day_by_day.afternoon: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — one of the Algarve's most iconic experiences. Paddle from Praia de Benagil through the turquoise waters and into the legendary Benagil Cave, a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight. The guided kayak tour takes approximately 2–3 hours. Alternatively, book a premium private boat tour for a more exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Sunset cocktails at the hotel or a rooftop bar. Dinner at a premium restaurant — try the tasting menu at a Lagos fine dining establishment, or enjoy a relaxed dinner at a wine bar with an extensive Portuguese wine list.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a Portimão restaurant near the waterfront — grilled sardines, ameijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams), local wine
meals.dinner: Premium Lagos restaurant — cataplana de peixe (fish cataplana), paired with a Quinta dos Vales Algarve red (~€55–70pp)

day_by_day.notes: Benagil is approximately 40 km east of Lagos (~40 min drive). Book the kayak tour in advance — morning slots are best for calmer seas and better light inside the cave. The cave can only be accessed by water. Wear a swimsuit and bring a waterproof bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, indulgent morning. Enjoy a long breakfast at the hotel, then visit a local spa in Lagos for a morning treatment — a traditional Portuguese massage or a sea-salt scrub. Alternatively, take a yoga or meditation session on the beach if offered by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the western Algarve — drive to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand at the dramatic clifftop lighthouse where the Atlantic stretches endlessly before you. Visit the Fortaleza de Sagres, a historic fortress with fascinating maritime history. The drive from Lagos is scenic and takes about 40 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset at Cabo de São Vicente — one of the most spectacular sunsets in Europe, as the sun drops into the Atlantic. Return to Lagos for a celebratory dinner at the best restaurant in town — book a premium tasting menu experience.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast with fresh fruit, local pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a Sagres restaurant — fresh grilled fish, local salads, and a glass of crisp Algarve white wine
meals.dinner: Premium tasting menu dinner in Lagos — 6-course menu with wine pairing (~€90–120pp)

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente is approximately 35 km west of Lagos (~40 min drive). The cape can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. Sunset at Cabo de São Vicente in mid-September is around 19:45–20:00 local time. Arrive 30–45 minutes early for the best spot.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Algarve wine country for a deeper exploration. Drive to Lagoa and visit Quinta dos Vales — one of the Algarve's most acclaimed wine estates. Take a private morning tour of the vineyards, sculpture garden, and wine cellar. Learn about the estate's award-winning wines and the unique microclimate of the Algarve interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine blending workshop at the quinta — work with the winemaker to create your own personalised blend, which can be bottled and labelled to take home as a unique souvenir. Follow with a premium wine and cheese lunch on the estate terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Lagos via the scenic EN125 road. Stop in Ferragudo — a picturesque fishing village with a castle, whitewashed houses, and a beautiful beach. Enjoy a sunset drink at a riverside café before returning to Lagos for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Wine and cheese pairing lunch at Quinta dos Vales — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, estate wines (included in workshop)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ferragudo or Lagos — grilled sea bream, local vegetables, Algarve wine (~€50–65pp)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales is approximately 25 km east of Lagos. Book the private wine blending workshop well in advance — it is a premium, exclusive experience. The bottled wine can be shipped home if you prefer not to carry it.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Lagos. Take a stand-up paddleboard lesson or guided SUP tour along the Lagos coastline — a wonderful way to see the sea caves and cliffs from the water. Alternatively, book a private sailing trip from Lagos marina for a half-day coastal cruise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Camilo — a stunning, intimate beach tucked between towering cliffs, accessible via a wooden staircase. Swim in the clear waters and explore the small sea caves at the base of the cliffs. Enjoy the relative seclusion compared to larger beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo at a Lagos rooftop bar or the hotel terrace. Dinner at a premium restaurant focusing on modern Portuguese cuisine — try dishes featuring local almonds, figs, carob, and fresh Atlantic fish in creative preparations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Praia do Camilo or a nearby clifftop restaurant — fresh seafood, local wine
meals.dinner: Modern Portuguese fine dining in Lagos — seasonal tasting menu with Algarve wine pairing (~€70–90pp)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is a short taxi ride or 20-minute walk from the hotel. The wooden staircase descent is steep — wear appropriate footwear. SUP lessons and sailing trips can be arranged through the hotel concierge or Lagos marina operators.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Alentejo wine region — a longer drive (~1.5 hours north) but well worth it for wine enthusiasts. Visit Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous near Beja for a premium winery experience. Tour the estate, vineyards, and olive groves with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a premium wine and food pairing lunch at the estate restaurant — Alentejo wines are among Portugal's finest, with bold reds and elegant whites. The estate restaurants offer exceptional farm-to-table cuisine using local produce. Browse the wine shop for bottles to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the early evening. Relax at the hotel. Final premium dinner at a top Lagos restaurant — a celebratory meal to mark the penultimate full day. Order the finest bottle of wine from the list and indulge in the best of Algarve seafood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — early start for the drive north
meals.lunch: Estate restaurant lunch at Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous — 3-course menu with wine pairing (~€60–80pp)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the finest Lagos restaurant — full tasting menu with premium wine (~€100–130pp)

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo day trip requires an early start — depart by 8:30am. Book the estate visit and lunch well in advance. Consider hiring a private driver for the day so both guests can enjoy the wine tasting fully. The drive through the Alentejo plains is beautiful and distinctly different from the coastal Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to a favourite beach or try somewhere new. Consider Praia da Luz, a charming village beach just 6 km west of Lagos, with calm waters and a relaxed atmosphere. Hire premium sun loungers and a parasol, order fresh juices and snacks from the beach bar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell boat tour — book a private catamaran or yacht charter from Lagos marina for a 3–4 hour afternoon cruise along the Algarve coast. Sail past the Ponta da Piedade rock formations, sea caves, and golden cliffs with a bottle of chilled Champagne or local sparkling wine on board. Swim from the boat in secluded coves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos marina at sunset. Final evening stroll through the old town. Farewell dinner at the best restaurant of the trip — a long, leisurely meal celebrating 13 days in the Algarve. Order a magnum of your favourite Algarve wine discovered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel
meals.lunch: Beach lunch at Praia da Luz — grilled fish, salads, local rosé
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant — full seafood feast, finest wines, dessert wines (~€100–150pp)

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran/yacht charters from Lagos marina typically cost €400–800 for a half-day private charter. Book in advance, especially on weekends. Praia da Luz is a 10-minute drive or 20-minute taxi from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel — savour every bite. Pack and check out. If time allows before the transfer, take one last walk along the Lagos city walls or sit at a café on Praça Gil Eanes with a final bica (espresso) and pastel de nata.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a private transfer to Faro Airport (approximately 1 hour). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for last-minute Portuguese souvenirs — wine, ginjinha, local ceramics, or Algarve almond sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve — golden cliffs, crystal waters, world-class wines, and the warmth of Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Boutique Taghostel — make it a long one
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lagos café before transfer, or at Faro Airport
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the hotel and arrange the airport transfer the evening before. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for the drive to Faro and airport procedures. Consider shipping any wine purchases home if luggage space is limited — the hotel concierge can assist with this.

query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London
